in_reply_to: not requested; arises from orbit-to-geminus-005 action 1 and from the smoke anomaly that held the swarm's first packet
title: Per-slot LoRA delivery and rollback on the RTX 3080, the runtime noise floor, what the shipped adapters do, zero-contrast design pairs, and target-residual preconditioning
summary: A. An adapter-sized shift reached every request in two server runs: 84 of 84 adapter requests and 36 of 36 W0 requests classified correctly by log-probability margin in each run. On this prompt the margin sees the formal-verification adapter only; the test does not show all three adapters were applied. 33 of 84 (run 1) and 16 of 84 (run 2) adapter requests still produced W0-like greedy text.

B. Q8_0 matmuls quantise their input activations to 8 bits on this backend (in the source, and measured for six matmuls). We infer this contributes to batch-composition noise, but the mechanism is incomplete: eight identical sequences in one batch still differ row to row. The cause is open. It sets a floor below which adapter effects cannot be observed.

Rollback. With the adapter verified to run on the prefix (corrected probe, 14 sequences), a last-layer FFN adapter rolls back exactly with no cache flush, 14 of 14 at k = 1, 4 and 16. Adapters at blk.28..30 leave a trace in KV and recurrent state that is still present 16 tokens later. The first probe's '16 of 16' for blk.31 was true by construction (no output rows on the prefix) and is kept only as a labelled replicate.
C. The shipped formal-verification adapter moves unrelated chat prompts as much as its own states, while the 24 anchors stay put.
D. Three of the eight design-pack training pairs carry a zero target and four more a mistimed one. The zero targets are established; their effect on those prompts was not tested.
E. Preconditioning the target residual with the gate metric roughly halves radial shrinkage at equal gain after compilation and is confirmed live, but raises KL on unrelated prompts. A mixed result.

A_per_slot_lora_delivery.claim: An adapter-sized shift reached every request of llama-server in two runs. On this prompt the margin sees the formal-verification adapter only, so the test does not show that all three adapters were applied. The earlier 'W0-like text on some slots' was a near tie at one token plus batch-composition noise.

server_level_logit_test.what: llama-server b12549, 8 slots, per-request 'lora' field, n_probs log-probabilities at the second generated token of the packet-009 smoke prompt. margin = logprob(```) - logprob(<think>).
server_level_logit_test.decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run: a request counts as 'adapters applied' when its margin is above the midpoint of the two single-request reference margins from the same server session
server_level_logit_test.what_the_margin_sees: Run 2 decoded single requests with each adapter subset. fv alone gives margin -0.1310 (adapter side of the threshold -0.3699); corpus alone -0.9252, design alone -0.5338, corpus+design -0.6341 (all W0 side). On this prompt the three-adapter margin therefore measures the formal-verification adapter's shift; it cannot distinguish 'all three applied' from 'fv applied alone'.
server_level_logit_test.effective_sample: The server never batches different adapter configurations together, so the 24 mixed-round results equal the two single-request references exactly and show config switching only. The effective sample in run 2 is 34 distinct adapter margins and 14 distinct W0 margins, not 84 and 36 independent draws.
server_level_logit_test.rounds: per run: 6 rounds of 8 concurrent adapter requests, 3 of 8 concurrent W0, 3 mixed (4 W0 + 4 adapter, alternating slots), 3 with staggered arrivals in three waves

library_level_probe.what: ctypes on the same llama.dll, adapters set context-wide, full logit vectors, three 8-sequence batch compositions. This does not exercise the server's per-request path; the test above does.

cross_checks_and_loose_ends: The server's single-request reference margins (-0.8180 and 0.0782) equal the library emulation of the prompt split 55+4 to four decimals (-0.8180 and 0.0782). That split was inferred from source; this confirms it.
In the strict text re-run (packet 009) rounds 0 and 1 showed slots 0,1,2,6,7 taking the W0-like branch, which is exactly the row set of the library's 8-sequence 55+4 emulation.

Round 2 of that re-run showed 7 of 8 W0-like after three arrival waves. No library emulation reproduces 7 of 8; the staggered rounds of the server-level test cover that arrival pattern and classify 24 of 24 correctly by margin.
The library's reconstruction of the first run's mixed batch predicts one W0-like row where that run showed two (the second has margin +0.0096).
All of this is one prompt and one token position.
A_per_slot_lora_delivery.recommendation: Test adapter application, rollback and 'adapter changes output' on logits or log-probabilities, not on greedy text. For an identical batch composition require an exact match; otherwise use a margin or delta-correlation test with a threshold set from reference requests.

B_activation_quantisation_and_noise_floo.claim: With Q8_0 weights the CUDA backend quantises the activation operand of quantised-weight matmuls to 8 bits per block of 32.
in_the_pinned_source: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/quantize.cu:89-90 d = amax / 127.0f; q = roundf(xi / d), over QK8_1 = 32 elements
ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu selects between these kernels by the number of rows in the batch

measured_for_six_matmuls.what: ffn_up, ffn_gate and ffn_down of blk.28 and blk.31, 372 single-sequence states: relative L2 error between a float64 reconstruction from the harvested input and the runtime's output

B_activation_quantisation_and_noise_floo.f16_lora_branch: The LoRA factors are F16, so their matmuls take the float path. Adapter deltas are computed on unquantised activations while the base is not. (Read from the source; not measured separately.)
B_activation_quantisation_and_noise_floo.link_to_batch_composition_noise: INFERRED, AND INCOMPLETE. Kernel choice depends on batch row count in the source, and the noise appears exactly when composition changes, but there is no unquantised control (an F16 GGUF of this model does not fit in 8 GiB). Eight identical sequences in one batch still differ row to row, which kernel choice by batch size cannot explain. Treat the cause of batch-composition noise as open.

identical_rows_in_one_batch.what: all8_whole variant: 8 identical W0 sequences decoded whole in a single batch, so every row shares one batch size and one kernel choice
identical_rows_in_one_batch.reading: The rows differ despite identical inputs and identical batch composition; the row-to-row spread is of the same order as the composition effect. Activation quantisation is measured, but it does not by itself explain this.

resolution_limit.final_residual: about 0.09 in norm, 0.2% of the radius. On the 24 anchors the measured change under the corpus adapter is 0.116 where exact arithmetic predicts 0.069.
resolution_limit.logits: 0.0 when an identical single-sequence decode is repeated; up to 0.26-0.46 across batch compositions on the example prompt; rows of one batch of 8 identical sequences also differ (fork-margin spread about 0.24)
resolution_limit.meaning: An adapter effect below these levels cannot be observed on this runtime. A leakage bound tighter than the floor is valid arithmetic with no observable consequence here.

weight_level.statement: After adapters are applied and removed, the base final residual is restored bit for bit when the batch composition is the same.
weight_level.scope: Each decode started from cleared memory. This is the scale-to-zero step of T-C5, not cache rollback.

mid_sequence_without_cache_flush.what: Corrected probe (v2): decode a prefix with one single-layer adapter on (scale 1), with an output row on every prefix token so the adapter runs on the prefix; switch it off WITHOUT clearing memory, decode k more tokens, compare logits with a run that never had the adapter. 14 sequences.

v1_replicate.caveat: The first probe (v1, 16 sequences) decoded the prefix with no output rows. This model evaluates the last-layer FFN on output rows only, so the blk.31 adapter never ran on the prefix and its '16 of 16 exact' was true by construction. The v1 blk.28..30 rows are kept as a replicate; the v1 blk.31 row carries no evidence about rollback.

mid_sequence_without_cache_flush.reading: With the adapter verified to run on the prefix (the blk.31 FFN adapter shifts prefix-end logits by a median of 1.6 to 1.9 while on), rollback without a cache flush is exact for 14 of 14 at k = 1, 4 and 16. Adapters at blk.28..30 leave a trace (median 0.10 to 0.30 logits across k), about the size of batch-composition noise, still present 16 tokens later. At these strengths the trace is small (KL below 1e-3, no top-token change).
mid_sequence_without_cache_flush.consequence: The cache-flush step of the rollback contract is necessary for earlier-layer adapters and unnecessary for last-layer ones. This is library level: llama-server already clears a slot's cache when its adapter configuration changes, so the server path does not exercise mid-sequence rollback without a flush.

C_shipped_adapters.what: The three composition adapters at mcproof 4552874 (each one rank-8 pair on blk.31.ffn_up), scale 1, measured live on 372 states and compared with the exact float64 prediction W_down (s * (B A x)).

selectivity_of_formal_verification_adapt.reading: It moves unrelated chat prompts about as much as its own training states and leaves the 24 anchors almost untouched. Preservation holds on the listed anchors and does not extend to their neighbours. n is 8 prompts per small pack.
selectivity_of_formal_verification_adapt.suggested_check: Measure preservation on off-domain prompts that were never preservation keys.

C_shipped_adapters.eta_note: Mean eta on own training states: formal-verification 0.029 (max 0.192), corpus 0.047, design 0.033. 0.01 is the default max_per_layer_radial_eta in weft tangent.py, not a rule the team set (the E8 arms use 0.20 and 0.05); these single-layer adapters were compiled without a per-layer cap.

D_design_pack_contrast_pairs.statement: In activation_harvester.py the corpus and design mini-packs take the first two tokens of the good and bad completions as the positive and negative token sets. For the design pack that makes 3 of 8 contrasts exactly zero, and 4 more depend only on the second token.
D_design_pack_contrast_pairs.consequence: exact_up_proj_swiglu_residual_f64 returns a zero residual when the contrast is zero. A zero target on a real key acts as a preservation constraint. The zero targets are established; their effect on those three design prompts was not tested. For the four partial pairs the target promotes the second token at the position that predicts the first.
D_design_pack_contrast_pairs.possible_link: In e8_qwen35_4b_live_tc1_receipt.json weft-eido has the smallest solo shift in the single-layer arm (0.002) and the lowest triple retention in both arms. This could contribute. We did not recompile the pack, and in the 4-layer arm its solo shift is not the smallest.
D_design_pack_contrast_pairs.fix: Take the first position at which the two completions differ, as the formal-verification path already does, or skip pairs with an empty contrast.

related_observation.statement: On the formal-verification decision states the base model often already agrees with the target.
related_observation.reading: The listed negatives are rarely the real competition. Weighting states by how contested they are, and choosing negatives from what the base actually prefers, are options.

E_target_residual_preconditioning.statement: The harvester builds the up-projection target as the contrast gradient pulled back by the transpose, du = s * (W_down^T g). That is the steepest-descent direction. Preconditioning with the gate metric M = W_down diag(s^2) W_down^T, du = s * W_down^T (M + lambda I)^-1 g, buys the same contrast gain with a smaller final-residual change.
E_target_residual_preconditioning.derivation: For a W_up edit at the last layer, dh = W_down (s * du) exactly. The plain choice gives dh = M g, whose energy per unit gain squared exceeds the minimum (dh parallel to g) by kappa = (g'M^2 g)(g'g)/(g'M g)^2.

stage_1_per_state_exact.what: single state, unconstrained du, exact float64, equal first-order gain of 1 logit; lambda in units of the mean eigenvalue of M; 'inf' is the plain target, '0' the minimum-norm one; KL over a top-32 support

stage_2_compiled_rank8.what: the team's BetaEdit projector with the P2-B recipe, 220 training states of 64 prompts, evaluated on 112 states of 32 held-out prompt ids in exact float64, every arm rescaled to the same mean gain; KL over a top-32 support

stage_3_live_gpu.what: the same compiled factors written as GGUF LoRAs and measured on the RTX 3080 at equal target gain; KL over the full vocabulary

what_improves_at_lambda_1: Radial shrinkage per unit gain squared: 0.00096 to 0.00047 live (0.49x), and the per-state median 0.00086 to 0.00041.
Log-probability of the positive token at equal contrast gain: +0.288 to +0.375 live.
Residual movement on unrelated corpus prompts: 0.0555 to 0.0353.
Live gain and eta match the float64 prediction to three or four digits at native scale.
what_gets_worse_or_does_not_improve: KL on unrelated corpus prompts RISES: 0.138 to 0.215 at lambda 1 and 0.295 at lambda 0.1, although the residual moves less. A smaller residual change is not a smaller change in distribution.
On-domain KL at equal gain does not improve: 0.612 plain, 0.628 at lambda 1, 0.736 at lambda 0.1, 0.710 minimum-norm.
Weight norm and K0 leakage at equal gain rise by about half at lambda 1 (3.174 to 4.664; 0.2666 to 0.3847), and the target is less low-rank (truncation error 0.436 to 0.553).
The unregularised minimum-norm target is worse once compiled: positive-token log-probability +0.172 live against +0.288 plain, at 8 times the weight norm.

lambda 10 improves the mean but not the per-state median of eta after compilation (0.003825 plain, 0.004291 at lambda 10): equal mean gain can hide redistribution across states (median gain 1.2153 plain, 3.23 at lambda 10).
E_target_residual_preconditioning.sizing: This is the gradient versus Gauss-Newton distinction applied to an edit that sits upstream of a gate and a down-projection. The principle is standard. What is offered is the identification in this pipeline and a three-stage measurement, with a mixed result: less shrinkage and more of the objective, more distribution change off-domain.
limits: blk.31 only, formal-verification states only, one split, safety directions not registered.

'Held-out' means held-out prompt ids (32 of 96, 0 overlap) inside the same four template families; 98% of held-out states reuse a (positive token, negative set) pair seen in training. The anchors evaluated are the compile-time preservation keys.
Stages 1 and 2 measure KL over a top-32 support; stage 3 over the full vocabulary.

reproducibility_note.statement: Two scripts that call the same compiler with the same inputs wrote byte-identical GGUF files. This shows the compile is reproducible on this machine and nothing more.

operational_note.statement: Loading llama.dll from another process fell back to CPU without any error, because ggml loads its CUDA backend with a plain native LoadLibrary that could not resolve cuBLAS. The first harvest ran on CPU with 0 MiB of VRAM in use until this was noticed; it was discarded and repeated.
operational_note.guard: The harness now asserts a registered GPU device, 'offloaded N/N layers' in the load log and a drop of over 1 GiB in free VRAM. Any tool that embeds llama.cpp and must run on the GPU should assert the same.

gpu_runs.note: Launched through mlos gpu-lease and mlos stamp-run; figures are the stamper's start and end snapshots.

review: Two independent review rounds recomputed this packet from raw files. All numbers reproduced. Round 1 raised findings on definitions and wording, including one claim that was wrong (off-domain KL); the server-level test and the rollback probe were added after that review. Round 2 confirmed those fixes and raised further points: the margin sees the formal-verification adapter only, the mixed rounds are serialised, the blk.31 rollback was true by construction (corrected probe re-run), the noise mechanism is incomplete, and wording items. The round-2 fixes were applied by the author; a third, narrow review of the revision is recorded in receipts/REVIEW_ROUND_3.md.
scrubbed: user paths and tailnet/LAN IPs replaced with placeholders; no keys or tokens. Raw logs are not shipped.
